findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB limit ignores admin-configured max upload sizes
findings.body: validateUploadedFile now uses a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, and the 413 handler at line 246 similarly hardcodes 10 MB instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. This silently disables the `max_image_size_kb` and `max_attachment_size_kb` site settings on the client: admins who set a lower limit will see users attempting uploads up to 10 MB (which then fail server-side with a confusing error for attachments), and admins who set a higher limit will get an incorrect 'file too large' rejection in the browser. This looks like leftover debug/test code (the PR description is 'Test 1') and should be reverted to read the settings.

findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently overrides the width/height variant
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145 and a second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149. In Ruby the second definition completely replaces the first, so the width/height variant is dead code. Any existing caller that invokes `downsize(from, to, width, height)` will now have its `height` argument bound to the `opts` parameter; when `optimize` evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer it raises `TypeError (no implicit conversion of Integer into Hash-like)`. Either remove the old signature entirely or rename/merge the two methods so the four-argument form still works.

findings.title: Downsize loop can never bring very large images under the limit and ignores downsize failures
findings.body: The retry loop runs at most 5 iterations, each downsizing to '80%', so the best possible reduction is to 0.8^5 ≈ 33% of the original size. An image more than ~3x `max_image_size_kb` will still exceed the limit when the loop exits, and the oversized file is then passed to `Upload.create_for`, which will reject it — the user waits through 5 ImageMagim/ImageOptim passes only to get the same failure the feature was supposed to prevent. Additionally, the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is never checked: if conversion fails (e.g. unsupported/corrupt image or ImageMagick policy limits), the loop blindly retries five times and may hand a truncated/corrupted tempfile to `Upload.create_for`. The loop should either compute the exact target percentage needed in one pass or check the downsize result and bail out with a clear error.

findings.title: allow_animation option never applies to uploads because animated-GIF detection relies on the file extension
findings.body: The controller passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but `OptimizedImage.optimize` (optimized_image.rb line 155) only chooses the animated code path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. The `from` path here is an uploaded/action-dispatched tempfile (RackMultipart-* or discourse-upload-*), which never ends in `.gif`, so animated GIFs are always processed through `convert #{from}[0]`, which takes only the first frame. Even on sites with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, every oversized animated GIF upload is silently stripped down to a single static frame — permanent loss of the original animation since the tempfile is downsized in place.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB download cap regresses API uploads for sites with larger configured limits
findings.body: The API URL-download path changed `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes`. On sites where an admin has raised `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 KB, remote images larger than 10 MB can no longer be fetched via the API at all (the download silently returns nil due to `rescue nil`, leading to a confusing failure downstream), even though such uploads were previously allowed. The cap should be derived from the setting (e.g. `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` plus some headroom to allow downsizing), not hardcoded.
